goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
goldens.reasoning: C1 and C8 both point to the stats update inside should_block? being a non-atomic read-modify-write that races under concurrent calls. That is the race-condition part of G1's concern about side effects during a check.

goldens.comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
goldens.reasoning: None of the candidates mention the unanchored domain regex that would let a subdomain bypass the whitelist.

goldens.comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
goldens.reasoning: C2 identifies the same issue: the case-sensitive lookup lets differently cased emails get past a block.

candidates: should_block? does a non-atomic read-modify-write (match_count += 1 then save) which can lose increments under concurrent calls, and ignores failed saves so stats updates can silently be dropped

Email comparisons in should_block? use exact lookup, but email comparisons elsewhere normalize via Email.downcase/strip, so case/whitespace variations can bypass a blocked entry. Should normalize the input

validate_each calls email_in_restriction_setting? and BlockedEmail.should_block? even when value is blank/nil, which can raise errors (e.g., nil =~ regexp). Should guard early with return if value.blank?
The model sets a default action_type in a callback, but the DB column has no default. Adding a database default would make manual/bulk inserts safer and align with the model's behavior
rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) creates a mutable array on the controller prototype that can unintentionally persist across controller reuse. Should initialize it per-instance in init

The computed property depends on rejectedEmails contents but uses rejectedEmails.@each which is for observing property changes on array items. Should use rejectedEmails.[] to reliably recompute when items are added/removed
The create endpoint now returns errors and values keys on failure, but there are no controller specs asserting this new response shape, so regressions could slip in
Should use atomic UPDATE ... match_count = match_count + 1 (e.g., update_all) for the stats update instead of read-modify-write
